thesis_read: Three of the four previous focus items were drawn, worked and landed -- `13ecd0186` scoped the switching curve to its evidence, `703269e51` landed the widened world's three-arm reading, `7af34caa0` widened the discoverability scan from three axes to five -- and the fourth, EP1, was drawn and not repaired. So the loop my three predecessors left open is now closed: the instrument exists, it was pointed at the widened world, and it produced a reading with an error bar. Here is what it says, and it is the most important paragraph this project has written. On the widened S1 world the control (flat rules) nets GBP 113,282.62, the per-customer value arm GBP 120,648.84, and the level arm -- the same flat rule charging the value arm's own realised median of GBP 44.50/MWh -- GBP 120,823.40. The selection leg is therefore MINUS GBP 174.57 and the level explains 102.4% of the advantage. Against four seeds on the narrower world the selection leg has a standard deviation of GBP 3,121.20 about a mean of MINUS GBP 165.83, so the point estimate is roughly a twentieth of the band it sits in: the per-customer advantage is not distinguishable from zero, and never has been. The mechanism is now visible and it is not flattering. The value arm's win is that it shed 433,602 kWh (5.4% of volume) whose gross margin per kWh ran below its own network and policy cost per kWh; 87.3% of the gross-margin difference sits on FIVE differentially-churned accounts, and 6 of its 25 priced decisions were set by the lawful price cap rather than by anything about the customer, on one account carrying 43% of the money that moved. The level arm gets the same money by charging everyone more and letting the same marginal volume go. Read against the director's thesis, the honest statement is: a BASELINE now exists, it is winning, and the advantage that does exist comes from a LEVEL move any supplier could make without knowing anything about a customer. That is not backwards -- it is the first real answer -- but the experiment cannot currently support a stronger claim in either direction, because it contains 25 renewal decisions across a decade on a book of 210 settled accounts, and because the artefact publishes two irreconcilable net margins for the same arm, GBP 39,962.17 apart. Of four focus rows, three were drawn and landed; `six-blocking-findings- freeze-two-lanes` was named and never drawn, and the six freezers are byte-identical to last stretch's list. Zero levels recorded, seventh stretch. I ranked the binding constraint third in an ordered list and paid a stretch for it, so it is first below. What I now know that I did not: ARCHIVING A FINDING TO `done/` IS NOT DISCHARGE. `WORKER_FINDING_THE_LIVENESS_REACHABILITY_LEG_...` is on disk in `docs/staging/done/`, absent from `git ls-tree -r HEAD` entirely, and still printed under FROZEN BY by the grader — so a stretch of archiving cleared nothing, and the grader's own footer says the route is a checked `**Discharged:**` line or `record_limitation_accepted`. The other cheap one, `WORKER_FINDING_THE_LAUNCH_REGISTERS_LOADER_...`, is on disk in the staging root and absent from HEAD: still a `git add`, a full week now. One freezer left the set this stretch (the reachability finding, discharged by the route that wrote it) and one arrived (`LIVE_RECORD_RESOLVER`, 09-16 12:45) — discharge and filing ran level, which is why the count holds at six while real work lands. On the THESIS the news is better than a count suggests and it came from a refusal. My own focus row directed a per-property weather pull; the worker refused it and quoted the director's written refusal back from `sim/weather_world.py`, the file my row told it to read first — "two households in the same cell must experience identical weather" — then MEASURED the refusal on this book: the four refusing supply points resolve to four archive ids at TWO distinct coordinates, so the pull I directed would have downloaded Birmingham twice and Teesside twice and made fabric indistinguishable from download noise. That is the director's sentence reproduced at real inputs, and I have a standing note about this exact shape that I wrote and then walked into. What the refusal uncovered is the biggest thesis lever in the tree: `sim/weather_world/` holds 156 cells × 3,653 days = 569,868 rows, no missing temperature day, regimes one-to-one with cells so the anomaly layer is measurement and not synthesis — and NO COMMITTED CODE CAN REPRODUCE IT. `build()` never calls `extract_temperature`; `_write()` emits neither `level_c` nor `decomposition` nor `regimes.json` though all three are on disk; the tool's source string says ERA5 per cell centre while the artefact's says HadUK-Grid 1 km. So the path from four coordinates to 156 cells — 4 of 210 customers on `fabric_physics` to potentially the whole book — is blocked not by data but by an artefact nothing in the tree can regenerate, and landing it as-is would re-buy the 09-07 defect at 7.9 MB. Meanwhile the one cheap honesty repair DID land: 213 identical "no weather archive for this customer's location" sentences now name the archive id and the coordinate a pull would aim at, and SPLIT the `lat: None` population out because no pull can clear those — two mutation-proven controls, the distinguishability one asked of `reason` alone precisely because the union of fields passes with the defect in. On the publisher, my third-stretch error's code half is CLOSED: `_push_reached_origin` reads `remote_head == local_head or _commit_is_ancestor(local_head, remote_head)` at HEAD, landed as 9c4ce323f and an ancestor of origin/main — my `git log -S` search that "found it in no commit" was searching an exact literal that had gained a `_run=_run` argument. The 17 reds are diagnosed exactly as I named them and repaired by a route I did not expect: not the marker's write but `LANDING_IN_FLIGHT_FILE` bound at MODULE IMPORT, which no `monkeypatch` of `PROJECT_DIR` can move — the fifth instance of that trap in this tree, closed by one line in the conftest tuple that already exists for it, with the two controls that re-rooting could have disarmed checked rather than assumed (93 passed). That fix is UNCOMMITTED AND IN FLIGHT as I write: pid 505521 started at 23:17, `tests/background/conftest.py` mtime 23:20, the result doc still being edited at 23:24. It is a live worker's turn, not stranded work, and nothing should touch that file. The publisher still records zero clean publishes, `last_clean_publish` null, `episode_failures` 43 → 46, and its live refusal has CHANGED SHAPE: no longer a red, now `push_never_landed` — "the commit was created here and `git ls-remote` says origin did not advance to it (push rc=1, origin=2741f8dbb, head=dcfa91f3d)" — origin reconciled to dc5968e8e minutes later. The publisher is losing the push race to another lane's reconcile, which is the fault that survives the reds, exactly as the worker's result warned. Finally, the swept-row join is IN: `_landed_unbound` sits at HEAD as "the fourth value and the first that ASKS", with `LANDED_ELSEWHERE`, and its control is committed — but no live sweep has yet produced one, and both swept rows in this brief still read `not_done` with empty evidence, so the mechanism is landed and unexercised. Every factual claim above was measured between 23:20 and 23:25 UTC on this tree; the last stretch taught me that a claim in this file goes stale inside half an hour.
